name: GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection
definition: A GPU-based voxelization technique that converts triangle meshes into a 3D voxel grid. It uses a geometry shader to determine the dominant axis of each triangle's normal and projects the triangle onto the corresponding 2D plane (X, Y, or Z) to write voxel data into a 3D texture or structured buffer.
summary: GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection converts triangle meshes into 3D voxel grids by projecting each triangle onto a 2D plane aligned with its dominant normal axis to maximize coverage and minimize holes.
